summary: The sole occurrence fits I.1 thinking/considering. The b ʕaqəl diḏe phrase locates the cognition in the fox's mind; it does not by itself establish a separate construction sense.

The inherited Preterit quotation already contains mgawmalle b-ʕaqəl diḏe and the ensuing hare visit, under prs 194/29. PrS 68/57 is therefore not a new independent example merely because the cell is thin.
The form remains in glossary stem I. Surface mgawmalle is compatible with assimilation of the root-final n before an L-agent suffix; no additional stem is introduced.
The inherited Kurdish nominal etymology and the finite Turoyo cognitive verb are retained. This token is not a light verb plus noun construction simply because its loan base is nominal.
The supplied translation includes going to the hare, whose Turoyo appears only in the reader's extended context, not in verse_turoyo. No new bilingual quotation is made from that boundary mismatch.
Reconcile prs 194/29 and PrS 68/57 with the edition's citation systems before changing the inherited reference.
Confirm the verse boundary for the hare visit: the supplied verse ends after mgawmalle b ʕaqəl diḏe, while its translation already includes going to the hare.
